newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called lower amid softer cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called lower amid softer cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open lower Tuesday following a weaker ACCESS session and early talk of softer cash, market sources said.
June over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.18 to $2.195 after settling to the downside Monday at $2.224 per million British thermal units.
On ACCESS, June last traded 2.5 cents weaker at $2.199 after retreating to a session low of $2.185.
Early cash prices at the Henry Hub were talked around $2.20, down at least five cents from Monday.

Technically, traders pegged support in June at $2.16-2.17, and then at $2.14 and $2.05, which is a double bottom and coincides with key trendline support. Resistance was seen at the contract high of $2.43 and then at $2.47-50.
Maintenance work on Transco's Texas line, which began Saturday, will cut the line's total capacity of about 600 mmcfd May 14-19, with 400 mmcfd still cut May 20-22.

But cooling demand in Texas is limited as most temperatures are hovering below normal. Temperatures throughout most of the East and Midwest are also forecast to average below normal through this week, with the coolest air evident in the upper Midwest. In the Southwest, warmer-than-normal weather is expected to persist over the next few days.

In Monday's cash market, Gulf Coast prices slipped a few cents to the low-to-mid $2.20s. Midcon pipes were down slightly to about $2.03-2.05. New York city gate gas also was modestly lower in the low-$2.50s.
Early estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association storage report are about 60-80 bcf, traders said.
